title: fix(agentsapi): bound silent native session startup
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Agents API continuations that remain silent until the outer turn watchdog expires when a saved native session never produces an event. Reusing the same binding can repeat the delay on every turn.

## User Impact

Native startup now fails after 120 seconds without an event, followed by the existing bounded native cleanup, with actionable inspection/reset guidance. Shorter attempt deadlines still apply. Existing bindings are retained and can continue when the service recovers; reset must settle old work before clearing a binding. Automatic replacement could abandon running work or lose hosted files that transcript replay cannot restore. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The attempt owner reuses the existing deadline controller for the cloud first-event window and disarms it after native event projection or settlement. HTTP acknowledgments and SSE keepalives do not satisfy it; legitimate native work after progress keeps its existing deadlines. Startup failure retires the native attempt while leaving the host turn able to deliver the error. Attempt-start and binding logs now include a bounded native session ID.

This leaves quiet-stream completion/reconciliation work in #161357 and completed-result recovery in #161322 separate. Production growth is 35 lines for the missing liveness boundary, cleanup-safe failure, and diagnostics; no cache, polling loop, schema, or alternate session owner is added. The test-line allocation covers the focused startup boundary suite and its shared completion fixture.

## Evidence

- On the exact main parent `cdd7ee54ee8df226291bb97a1077731f40fbd273`, all three regression cases fail at 120 seconds of virtual time: stalled reasoning update, stream connection, and first event. The active-native-work control passes. Base command wall: 24.49 seconds.
- Candidate proof exercises real attempt/session owners and SQLite binding lifecycle with controlled native I/O, including cancellation after submitted input, host error-delivery authority, binding preservation across restart, and continuation after service recovery. The focused attempt/session/persistence suites passed 61 tests in 141.11 seconds. After extraction, all 29 existing persistence cases passed; the final four-case startup suite passed in 67.07 seconds including 36.27 seconds of cold worker compilation (29.80 seconds on the preceding warm run).
- A live synthetic hosted session held at `requires_action` accepted a reasoning update in 589 ms and accepted another input, rather than returning a busy error. Subscription opened in 556 ms. Cancellation was observed settled to idle before the task-owned session was deleted. This verifies busy-session contracts; it does not reproduce a server-internal wedge or inspect an operator's native session.
- Final Codex autoreview is scoped-clean at P0–P2. `pnpm check:changed --staged --timed` completed: production types, boundaries, formatting, script lint, storage guards and other selected checks passed. Its test-fixture type and lint findings were fixed, and both targeted checks pass. The remaining dead-export failures reproduce verbatim on exact main parent `cdd7ee54ee8d`: all 32 production entries and all 10 full-tree entries match. Causal attribution follows the export/consumer migrations in #196207, #192552, #130634, #190544, #191513, #196252, #191326, #121929, #190205, #132716, #139911, #129184, and commits `832bbf926fc5` / `a7436c8b4a93`; these are main regressions, not a passing gate. The first PR CI found an incomplete logger mock in the instructions suite and a session mock that omitted real exports; both fixtures are corrected. All 34 affected instruction/startup cases pass in 55.44 seconds and the mock-export ratchet passes. No production change was needed for these CI repairs. Final-head CI run [42783810599](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42783810599) passed every primary job except `check-docs` and its aggregate gate. That failure is four unrelated release-tooling formatting defects, reproduced on exact CI main parent `19aa98b9258b` and causally introduced by `09723cdcad18` / #196501. The four blobs are unchanged in the tested PR merge; this is a new main regression, not a PR-caused failure. ClawSweeper completed final-head `c7051cbafb81` review with zero findings/open items.
- Exploratory owner-cost benchmark: five interleaved A/B runs across 10,000 synthetic session identities measured one added timer at approximately 0.88 microseconds CPU and 2,248 sampled allocated bytes per turn. A/A variation was 5.7% CPU and 3.2% allocation. This is correctness overhead, not a throughput improvement. The changed owner does no database/workspace scanning; this measurement does not qualify a 35 GiB SQLite database or Linux/btrfs workload.

No deployment or live-state repair was performed. No browser-imported module changed.

Inherited CI detail: `scripts/lib/full-release-child-reuse.mjs`, `test/scripts/full-release-receipt-recovery.test.ts`, `test/scripts/plugin-npm-cli-process.test.ts`, and `test/scripts/plugin-npm-cli-recovery.test-support.mjs` fail the same scoped formatter on `19aa98b9258b`. The two existing files are clean before #196501 and fail after it; the other two were introduced unformatted. Native admission will retain run 42783810599 attempt 1, tested merge `fb54cb0e4c761d138f73a478dedcaf3b007d9df0`, and failed job 129720801194 rather than claiming green CI.
